severity_rubric: PROPOSED (the token-parity-audit skill is not in the repo yet). P1 = a colour that carries meaning (status/severity) differs. P2 = the same role uses a different token or value, or a token is stale/hardcoded where the other side binds. P3 = naming, scale or hygiene with little visible difference.
scope: mapped token values vs relationship; bound vs hardcoded fills; text styles; semantic state colours. No layout or screenshot comparison.

findings.title: Severity and status colours use different tokens and values
findings.evidence: Mobile uses local priority level/* tokens (critical #ef4444 Red/500, high #fb923c Orange/400, medium #facc15 Yellow/400, low #38bdf8 Sky/400, minimal #a1a1aa) and never binds color-icon-warning or color-icon-success. Web uses AOH status tokens: color-icon-error/-warning/-info/-success, color-bg-warning-strong (~6,800 uses, mostly map pins and clusters), and color-border-warning/-warning-muted. No value matches: AOH error is Red/600, warning is Yellow/500, info is Blue/600.

findings.title: Web uses a hardcoded orange with no AOH token
findings.evidence: #f97316 (Orange/500) appears as 30% fill + stroke vectors and ellipses in all 8 web modules. Mobile's nearest colour is priority level/high #fb923c (Orange/400). Confirm what the orange means, then give it one token on both sides.

findings.title: Active, selected and link states use different token families
findings.evidence: Mobile marks these states with color-*-interactive tokens: icon-interactive 1,168 on Chat, border-interactive 386 on Comms, text-interactive on all pages. Web barely uses -interactive (icon 62 on Chat, border 19 on Responder) and uses color-*-primary and color-bg-info-strong instead. This is inferred from usage counts; check one component pair (e.g. Panel/ Tab vs Tab bar) before fixing.

findings.title: Focus ring uses different tokens
findings.evidence: Mobile uses color-border-focusRing-sidebar (Zinc/400, a sidebar token) on Recent, Chat and Map, and color-border-interactive-focus (Sky/500). Web uses AOH color-border-focusRing (Blue/500). Recommendation: mobile adopts color-border-focusRing.

findings.title: Card corner radius differs (8px vs 12px)
findings.evidence: Web binds Radius/radius-card (12px) on Chat (483) and Login. Mobile never uses radius-card; its cards use radius-dialog (8px) or hardcoded radius 8 / 20.

findings.title: Mobile binds to stale collections .Semantic and Dimensions
findings.evidence: These collections are not in AOH and not published by any library linked to the file, so their values are frozen. Used on all 7 scanned mobile pages, e.g. Spacing/input-size-container-md, Spacing/px, Spacing/0.5. Spacing/spacing-2xs and spacing-lg duplicate AOH names. Rebind to AOH Spacing.

findings.title: Web binds to the same stale collections
findings.evidence: The same .Semantic and Dimensions variables are used in all 8 web modules, plus web-only Spacing/1.5, 3.5, Border Radius/rounded, rounded-lg, rounded-none, Radius/rounded-sm and a misspelled Spacing/input-size-containr-sm. Rebind to AOH Spacing.

findings.title: Avatar is a different component with different tokens
findings.evidence: Web uses the AOH Avatar component, Size/size-avatar-xs/sm/md and AOH Avatars/* images. Mobile uses a local Avatar component with the local token comms/avatar-surface (#2a3f5c) and no avatar size tokens.

findings.title: Web Login has hardcoded text and border colours
findings.evidence: #09090b and #71717a text plus #e4e4e7 strokes match color-text, color-text-muted and color-border (Light) but are not bound. Also #ffffff at 40% and a non-AOH paint style 'Gradient - Dark'. Web Login: 90.2% bound. Mobile Login: 98.5%.

findings.title: Icons on dark surfaces use different tokens
findings.evidence: Web uses color-icon-invers (~2,200 uses, map pins and chips). Mobile never uses it; it uses color-icon-onColor. Values differ: invers is Gray/200 (Light), onColor is Zinc/50.

findings.title: Input borders use a different token name (same value)
findings.evidence: Web binds color-border-input. Mobile binds color-border. Both resolve to Zinc/200 / Zinc/800 today, so nothing looks different yet, but they will drift if either is changed.

findings.title: Both platforms use gap 10, which is off the AOH spacing scale
findings.evidence: gap 10 is unbound on both: mobile Chat 469, Comms 305; web Chat 627, Responder 366. The AOH scale has 8 and 12, not 10. Web also leaves padLeft 12 unbound in every module (spacing-md exists). Either add 10 to AOH or move both platforms to 8/12.

findings.title: Web Chat uses 10px text, below the AOH minimum
findings.evidence: Geist Regular 10, unstyled, appears 240 times in web Chat. The smallest AOH text style is text-xs (12px).

findings.title: Title text styles differ
findings.evidence: Mobile titles use ShadCN typography/h1-h2 and text-xl/font-bold (Login). Web panels use text-lg/font-bold, and web Login uses ShadCN typography/h3.

expected_platform_differences: Mobile uses size-button-lg/xl and size-input-lg (touch targets). Web uses size-button-sm, size-input-sm and size-formControll-sm. Not drift.
spacing-xs and spacing-3xl are used only on web.
excluded: Android-nav-bar, keyboard and keyboard kit (OS-drawn UI)
